cases.purpose: BASHVEC_BACKEND=scalar, sse2 and avx2 each select that backend and `vec backend` reports it, in a fresh shell per value, with auto/unset/empty choosing avx2 on an AVX2 guest.
cases.oracle: Guest /proc/cpuinfo flags (independent CPU feature oracle) and the documented BASHVEC_BACKEND override: scalar/sse2/avx2 select that backend, auto and unset select the widest the CPU supports.
cases.comparison: Candidate output, status and files compared with values derived independently of candidate output.
cases.script:
has=no
while read -r k rest; do [[ $k == flags* && " $rest " == *" avx2 "* ]] && has=yes; done < /proc/cpuinfo
echo "cpu-avx2=$has"
for be in scalar sse2 avx2 auto bogus; do
  printf '%s -> ' "$be"; BASHVEC_BACKEND=$be "$BASH" --noprofile --norc -c 'vec backend'
done
printf 'unset -> '; "$BASH" --noprofile --norc -c 'unset BASHVEC_BACKEND; vec backend'
printf 'empty -> '; BASHVEC_BACKEND= "$BASH" --noprofile --norc -c 'vec backend'
cases.stdout:
cpu-avx2=yes
scalar -> scalar
sse2 -> sse2
avx2 -> avx2
auto -> avx2
bogus -> scalar
unset -> avx2
empty -> avx2

cases.purpose: Exact integer and dyadic-float sum, min, max and dot over i32/u32/i64/f32/f64 vectors of 1..129 elements (full 4/8-lane blocks plus scalar tails) agree with an independent Python scalar model under every backend selection.
cases.oracle: Independent Python model of sum/min/max/dot over the same deterministic cells (integer arithmetic, or exactly representable x.5 floats formatted with C %g / %.17g), computed outside the candidate.
cases.comparison: Candidate output, status and files compared with values derived independently of candidate output.

files.run.sh:
be=$1
for t in i32 u32 i64 f32 f64; do
  for n in 1 2 3 4 5 7 8 9 15 16 17 31 32 33 63 64 65 127 128 129; do
    a=(); b=()
    for ((i=0;i<n;i++)); do
      x=$(( (i*37+11)%201-100 )); y=$(( (i*53+7)%97-48 ))
      [[ $t == u32 ]] && { x=$((x+100)); y=$((y+100)); }
      if [[ $t == f32 || $t == f64 ]]; then x=$x.5; y=$y.5; fi
      a[i]=$x; b[i]=$y
    done
    vec from-array -T $t a -h ha; vec from-array -T $t b -h hb
    printf '%s %s %s sum=%s min=%s max=%s dot=%s\n' "$be" $t $n "$(vec sum $ha)" "$(vec min $ha)" "$(vec max $ha)" "$(vec dot $ha $hb)"
    vec free $ha; vec free $hb
  done
done

cases.script: for be in scalar sse2 avx2 auto; do BASHVEC_BACKEND=$be "$BASH" --noprofile --norc ./run.sh $be || echo "run $be failed"; done
